gaps.description: Monthly spend ceiling is still TBD, so the gate-spend-ceiling.sh pre-hook on `confirmed` blocks deterministically; the confirmed gate cannot pass as written.
No document gives the ScientistTwo site URL, gallery location, or PDF host, so the agent must guess or web-search the primary data source.

Target count is ambiguous: ConOps cites 86 papers beating SOTA on 107 problems, and 'every generated paper' could mean either figure, or all generated papers including the ones that did not beat SOTA.

The acceptance check (discovered count matches the site, or the difference is explained in 'inventory notes') is enforced by no gate check, and 'inventory notes' could mean the per-row notes column or a separate file.

The provenance record's key names and format (`path`, `url`, `retrieved` as YYYY-MM-DD, `sha256`) are defined only in the check_provenance.py docstring, not in SPEC, FND-C-02, or docs/03; SPEC omits the required `path` key, so a SPEC-faithful implementation can fail the gate.
Nothing says what test_FND_C_02_* must assert, or that it must avoid live network access; a networked test would make gate-tests.sh flaky at every later gate.

Parent-paper PDFs are needed for the compute estimate ('the paper's setup section'), but no feature says whether to download them, where to put them, or how to record their provenance; which paper's setup section counts (generated or parent) is also ambiguous.
No data dictionary: `reported_gain_pct` (gain over what, from which source) has no basis in any doc, and the allowed values for `compute_class` and `candidate_for_p3` are not enumerated or validated.
The 'unknown' convention does not separate 'no public code' from 'not determined', so the code-availability rate (the exit criterion that drives the R1 decision) cannot be computed reliably.
Acceptance requires only that `candidate_for_p3` is filled on every row; nothing checks that 2 to 3 candidates are actually flagged, as the docs/07 exit criterion requires.

No acceptable error-rate threshold is defined, and the requirement to record the rate in docs/reviews/incr-0.md is not enforced by check_inventory.py; that file only exists at the later incr0_review gate.
It is unclear whether Budget.charge() and a BudgetExceeded exception (a docs/03 comment) are in scope for Increment 0, and 'every docs/03 model round-trips' should exclude the JudgeBackend Protocol.

StageResult says its gate Verdict is 'issued by a different component' but gives no validation rule (gate.judge_id != StageResult.producer_id), so the no-self-grading rule is enforced only on Verdict itself.
check_schema_version.py requires a literal `SCHEMA_VERSION = "X.Y"` line in vera/schemas/__init__.py; a value re-exported from a submodule would fail the check, and SPEC does not say so.

T3 has no scoring rubric or ground truth for 'reference-list accuracy' and 'table fidelity', does not say who scores (agent or Chris), and does not address the Windows setup cost of GROBID (Java/Docker) or the spend on an LLM-extraction option.
Acceptance says 'with scores', but check_trade_decided.py checks only the heading status and the **Decision:** and **Reverse if:** lines, not that scores are recorded.
'Set the TBD targets that the inventory informs' does not name which TBDs; most (JDG-P, AUD-P) need Increment 1/2 benchmark data, which invites invented numbers.

The exit criterion 'decide whether P1 v1 includes method-code checks' is not an explicit deliverable of any feature, and 'Monthly spend ceiling set' is covered only by the confirmed hook, not by SPEC.

The referenced Meridian scripts (validate-contract.sh, validate-spec.sh, run-evaluator.sh, gate-engine.sh, features-init.sh, dogfood.sh) are absent from scripts/, so the confirmed and incr0_review hooks cannot run until Meridian installs them.
MOE-1 to MOE-3 are qualitative ('substantially', 'meaningful fraction') and every linked requirement target is TBD, so project-level success is not yet measurable.
Where the project runs and publishes (local Windows workstation, optional cloud GPU, arXiv/workshop papers, public results table) is only implied through ConOps and docs/07, not stated.
These columns duplicate data/provenance.jsonl, and no check keeps the two consistent.
The inventory has one row per generated paper, but compute class is defined per parent problem, and the mapping between papers and problems (1:1 or not) is unstated.

contradictions.description: CONTRACT and the confirmed gate require the spend ceiling before `confirmed`; ConOps §4 says 'suggest setting one before Increment 1'; CONTRACT says docs/ wins when they disagree.
docs/07 lists 'Monthly spend ceiling set' as an Increment 0 exit criterion (end of increment), but gates.yaml enforces it at the very first gate.
docs/02 says TBD values are set at the end of Increment 0, while docs/07 Increment 1 says JDG-P targets are 'set from data' in Increment 1.
SPEC says to prefer a published listing over reverse-engineering page requests; docs/07 task 2 tells the agent to inspect page source and network requests.
SPEC and FND-C-02 name three provenance fields (URL, retrieval date, SHA-256); the check also requires `path` and the exact key `retrieved`.
SPEC names check_inventory.py as the check that the error rate is recorded in docs/reviews/incr-0.md; the script only prints the rate.

overall_notes: The confirmed gate cannot pass as written because the ConOps spend ceiling is TBD, and the docs disagree on when it must be set; the ScientistTwo source URL and the target paper count are undefined for the agent. Both fixes are cheap (set the ceiling, add the site URL, count definition, provenance record format and an inventory data dictionary including code-unavailable vs unknown), after which the remaining gaps rate a warn.
